take_homes: Don't build for the sales team first. Check who would maintain it and who it is for, because I've been shopping for a use of my platform.
The agent file is a shell. The value is in the memory and corrections, and accountability doesn't copy, so a shared agent needs a named owner.
Ask 'what would have to be true for them to switch?' and write the failure story before I build.

monday.move: Don't build the weekend sales setup yet. Ask the head of sales how they prepare for a customer call today, and ask who would own the agent if it existed.
monday.who: Head of sales, plus one sales rep they trust
monday.stop_condition: If they don't name a job they'd give up their current way for, or nobody will own it, I don't build it.
monday.blocker: The urge to just build it over the weekend, and finding the 20 minutes in the week.

misconception.why: I still think the agent's output is mostly fine and I'd skip review on my own work. But the point that accountability doesn't copy, and the leadership story where good analysis went nowhere, made me see that the problem is who checks and owns it, not how good the model is. The module never made me run a real check, so it's only shaken.

one_line: Less hands-on than I wanted, but the 'you can't share an agent, only context, a skill, output or an interface' bit and the missing-names bit hit. I'd send the non-engineering leads, not my engineers.
